verdict.summary: You can register a bexio OAuth app yourself in the Developer Portal with only a bexio account (a trial is enough) and by accepting the terms. None of the sources describe a review step, a test mode or an install cap for portal apps. The catches are contractual. Once 5 or more bexio accounts are connected to an independent business built on the API, you must send bexio a self-declaration. A Marketplace listing is optional and needs at least 10 bexio customers, at least 20 active users, OIDC login and content in four languages.
verdict.hands_on_effort: 30-60 min for the app and Composio setup; several days of work if you go for a Marketplace listing
verdict.time_to_first_connection: 15-30 min (if you already have a bexio account)
verdict.approval_wait: none documented for the OAuth app. The Marketplace listing review has no published timeline.

gates.name: Developer Portal app (your own bexio account)
gates.unlocks: Connect your own bexio company through your own client ID and secret.
limits: Needs a bexio account. The docs say a trial account is enough.
You must accept the developer portal terms, including section 4.4 on commercial use.
API access is limited by both the granted scopes and the bexio user rights of the person who connects.

gates.unlocks: Other bexio users and companies can authorize the app, provided its callback URL is registered. None of the sources describe a test-user allowlist or test mode.

Up to 10 redirect URLs per app.
Refresh tokens (offline_access) expire after 1 year without use.
Per-minute rate limit per company (HTTP 429). The official numbers were not found.

gates.name: Public use / bexio Marketplace listing
gates.unlocks: Anyone can connect, and none of the sources mention a review for that. A Marketplace listing (optional) adds visibility in bexio's marketplace.

Marketplace listing: at least 10 bexio customers in your regular clientele, at least 20 active users, OIDC login, customer support, app in 2 languages, marketplace content in DE/FR/IT/EN, and a signed partner agreement.
bexio can restrict API access for good cause at any time.
gates.time_to_reach: No review for public use. The Marketplace listing has no published timeline.

steps.title: Create a bexio account
steps.detail: Sign up at www.bexio.com (a trial account is enough according to the API docs) and complete the onboarding. Use a bexio user with enough rights for the data your agent needs, because API calls run with that user's rights.
gotchas: Make's guide says to create a paid account. The official docs only require an account, so check this if the portal refuses a trial account.

steps.title: Log into the Developer Portal and accept the terms
steps.detail: Go to developer.bexio.com, log in with your bexio credentials, then read and accept the terms and conditions. Pay attention to section 4.4 on commercial use: an independent business model with 5 or more connected bexio accounts requires a self-declaration.

steps.title: Create the app and register the redirect URL
steps.detail: Create a new app with your product name, your company URL and the allowed redirect URL. Paste the exact callback URL shown in your Composio auth config. It must match exactly, because bexio rejects unknown redirect URLs during authorization.

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

gotchas: Up to 10 redirect URLs per app.
Composio has both a v1 and a v3 callback path. Register whichever one your auth config shows.

steps.title: Copy the client ID and client secret
steps.detail: Open the app in the portal and copy its Client ID and Client Secret. Keep the secret server-side only, because the code exchange requires it.

steps.title: Choose a minimal scope list
steps.detail: Trim Composio's default list of about 37 scopes to what your agent needs. Keep openid and offline_access, and use only the edit scope where you need writes, because a write scope also grants read on that resource. Scopes are separated by spaces.
gotchas: Adding scopes later means every user has to authorize again. A refresh never widens scopes.
In June 2026 bexio changed the required scopes for purchase bill, payment and expense endpoints. Check the current docs for those endpoints.

steps.title: Configure the Composio auth config
steps.detail: In Composio, create a bexio auth config of type OAUTH2 (Composio has no managed bexio app). Enter the client ID, client secret and your trimmed scopes. Composio's role is the same as other brokers' that take a developer's bexio credentials and callback URL.

steps.title: Run a test authorization with your own account
steps.detail: Start a connection from Composio and complete consent on auth.bexio.com, then make a read call such as listing contacts. If you see 'Client nicht gefunden', the client ID is wrong. A redirect error means the callback URL does not match exactly.

steps.title: Create a separate production app
steps.detail: bexio recommends a separate client ID and secret for production. Create a second app in the portal with the production Composio callback URL, and point your production auth config at it.

steps.title: Connect other bexio companies
steps.detail: Send other users the Composio connect link. None of the sources mention an allowlist or review. Each user's access is limited by their own bexio user rights. Handle HTTP 429 rate-limit responses and the RateLimit headers.

steps.title: File the self-declaration once 5+ accounts are connected
steps.detail: If your product is an independent business model built on the bexio API and 5 or more bexio accounts are connected, email marketplace@bexio.com with your business model and the number of connected accounts. bexio then decides whether to offer a partnership agreement.
gotchas: If you skip this or decline a partnership, bexio may restrict your API use or charge a fee.

steps.title: (Optional) Apply for a Marketplace listing
steps.detail: Only if you want a listing: fill out the form on the 'Become a marketplace partner' page. You need at least 10 bexio customers in your regular clientele, at least 20 active users, OIDC login, customer support, the app in 2 languages and marketplace content in DE/FR/IT/EN. You also sign the marketplace partner agreement.

steps.title: Wait for bexio's Marketplace decision
steps.detail: bexio publishes no review timeline or criteria beyond the listed requirements. Your app keeps working for users while you wait, because the listing is not required for public connections.

Issues a refresh token so the connection outlives the user's session. The offline session expires after 1 year without use.
Write access that also grants read on the same resource, so you can drop the matching *_show scope. None of the sources mention a scope-level review.
Read-only access per object. Adding scopes later requires the user to authorize again.

blockers.symptom: Authorization error after consent / redirect rejected
blockers.cause: The redirect URL is not registered on the bexio app, or does not match it exactly (e.g. Composio v1 vs v3 callback path).
blockers.fix: Copy the exact callback URL from the Composio auth config into the app's redirect URLs in the Developer Portal.
Re-copy the Client ID from the Developer Portal into Composio.

blockers.symptom: API use restricted or a fee charged by bexio
blockers.cause: An independent business model with 5 or more connected accounts and no self-declaration, or a declined partnership.

blockers.symptom: Connection stops refreshing; the user must reconnect
blockers.cause: The refresh token went unused for 1 year, or offline_access was not requested.
blockers.fix: Request offline_access and refresh tokens periodically.

blockers.symptom: New endpoints return permission errors after a scope change
blockers.cause: Refresh does not add scopes, or the bexio user lacks rights for that data.
blockers.fix: Have the user authorize again with the new scopes, and check the user's bexio rights.
Back off using the RateLimit headers.

composio.note: Composio has no managed OAuth app for bexio. It offers only an OAUTH2 auth config (bring your own client ID and secret) and a BEARER_TOKEN mode. The bearer token (a personal access token) is only for your own account, because bexio requires the authorization code flow when other parties connect. Register your own app in the bexio Developer Portal, add the exact Composio callback URL shown in your auth config (v1 and v3 paths differ) as a redirect URL, and trim the default list of about 37 scopes to what you need.

evidence.claim: bexio's API docs set out the setup order: sign up, log into the developer portal, accept the terms, create an app with redirect URLs, then read the client ID and secret.
evidence.quote: Go to the developer portal at https://developer.bexio.com and log in using your bexio credentials.

evidence.claim: An app may register up to 10 redirect URLs.
evidence.quote: Up to 10 different redirect URLs can be defined for an app, e.g. to support multiple test environments and mobile apps with custom schemes.

evidence.claim: A community guide says the redirect URL must match the portal entry exactly.
evidence.quote: it has to match the Developer Portal exactly, otherwise sign-in stops with an error message.

evidence.claim: bexio advises using a separate client ID and secret for production.
evidence.quote: Please make sure to always use a separate set of Client ID and Client Secret for production environments.

evidence.claim: The developer portal is publicly reachable and titled 'bexio Developer Portal'.
evidence.quote: bexio Developer Portal

evidence.claim: The authorize endpoint rejects an invalid client_id with a 'client not found' error.
evidence.quote: Something went wrong. Client nicht gefunden.

evidence.claim: bexio publishes its OIDC endpoints under the /realms/bexio path.
evidence.quote: Authorization endpoint | https://auth.bexio.com/realms/bexio/protocol/openid-connect/auth

evidence.claim: The code exchange requires the client secret, so the app must be server-side.
evidence.quote: Your app must be server-side because during this exchange, you must also pass along your application's Client Secret

evidence.claim: Multiple scopes are separated by spaces.
evidence.quote: Multiple scopes have to be separated by a whitespace.

evidence.claim: The docs' setup steps require only a bexio account, and a trial account is enough.
evidence.quote: Create a bexio account by signing up for a trial account at https://www.bexio.com and complete the onboarding process.

evidence.claim: A write scope also grants read on the same resource.
evidence.quote: Read access is granted automatically when a write scope is requested for a resource.

evidence.claim: Scopes come in per-object show and edit pairs.
evidence.quote: kb_invoice_edit Write access to invoices

evidence.claim: offline_access yields a refresh token.
evidence.quote: offline_access Ensures that tokens can be refreshed also after the current user session has been closed.

evidence.claim: New scopes require the user to go through authorization again.
evidence.quote: Acquiring new scopes is only possible by going through the initial authorization process again.

evidence.claim: API access runs with the user rights of the person who connected.
evidence.quote: The API access happens with the user rights of the user who set up the connection to the application.

evidence.claim: No bexio scope is labelled sensitive or restricted, and no scope-level review appears in any source reviewed.
Offline sessions have a one-year idle timeout.
evidence.quote: Offline sessions will have an idle timeout of 1 year.

evidence.claim: A Marketplace listing needs at least 10 bexio customers among the developer's regular clientele.
evidence.quote: At least 10 bexio customers (SMEs or fiduciaries) among your regular clientele.

evidence.claim: A Marketplace listing needs at least 20 active users.
evidence.quote: At least 20 active users of your app.

evidence.claim: Marketplace partners must integrate through the API, offer OIDC login and provide customer support.
evidence.quote: Integration via bexio API and OpenID Connect login.

evidence.claim: The developer must accept the portal terms, and the docs point to section 4.4 on commercial use.
evidence.quote: Read and accept the terms and conditions (please pay special attention to the commercial use regulations mentioned in Section 4.4).

evidence.claim: Marketplace content must be in 4 languages and the app in at least 2.
evidence.quote: app in two languages, marketplace content in all four.

evidence.claim: Marketplace partners sign a partner agreement.
evidence.quote: You sign the marketplace partner agreement.

evidence.claim: Marketplace entry starts with a form, and no review timeline is given.
evidence.quote: Simply fill out the form so that we can get to know your solution better

evidence.claim: A third-party guide says a Marketplace listing requires OIDC login.
evidence.quote: if you want to be listed in the bexio Marketplace, you must also implement OpenID Connect (OIDC) for SSO login via bexio.

evidence.claim: Personal access tokens are for a user's own use; apps that other parties connect must use the authorization code flow.
evidence.quote: If you have a use case that requires the sharing of access tokens with another party, you must use the Authorization Code Flow instead.

evidence.claim: A community guide says the API returns 429 when a per-minute limit per company is exceeded.
evidence.quote: the API limits requests per minute and company.

evidence.claim: The changelog records a rate-limiting section that explains the RateLimit headers.
evidence.quote: Added rate limiting section that explains RateLimit HTTP headers.

evidence.quote: If a customer operates an independent business model, based on the provider's API, in which at least five (5) bexio accounts are connected, the customer is obliged to make a self-declaration.

evidence.claim: No install cap, user limit or unreviewed-app restriction appears in the sources reviewed.
The 2026-06-19 changelog changes the required scopes for purchase bill, payment and expense endpoints.
evidence.quote: Required scopes updated for purchase bills, payment and expense endpoints.

open_questions: Does bexio review a Developer Portal OAuth app beyond the terms you accept? None of the sources document this, and no install cap was found either.
Does creating a portal app need a paid bexio plan? The docs say a trial is enough, but Make's guide says to create a paid account.
Does the portal accept Composio's callback URL? This was not tested. The redirect URL rules (HTTPS-only, localhost) are also unconfirmed.
Is PKCE supported? This is unconfirmed, and the realm-scoped OIDC discovery URL was not probed.
What are the official per-minute rate-limit numbers? They were not retrieved.
The separate developer portal terms (section 4.4) were not fetched directly, and the current versions of the GTC documents were not verified.
How long does a Marketplace listing review take? No timeline or criteria are published beyond the listed requirements.
